Found the bug: in `_flatten_up_to_token`, the break condition is inverted. It currently reads `if not (t == token): break` which breaks on the very first token that doesn't match (basically always breaking immediately unless the first token happens to equal target), instead of yielding tokens until the target token is reached. This miscalculates offsets used throughout reindentation (e.g. `_get_offset`), causing wrong indentation/newline decisions as seen in the parenthesis/where/identifier-list regressions. I'll fix the condition to break when the token matches (and yield otherwise), matching correct upstream behavior.

It currently reads `if not (t == token): break` which breaks on the very first token that doesn't match (basically always breaking immediately unless the first token happens to equal target), instead of yielding tokens until the target token is reached. This miscalculates offsets used throughout reindentation (e.g. `_get_offset`), causing wrong indentation/newline decisions as seen in the parenthesis/where/identifier-list regressions. I'll fix the condition to break when the token matches (and yield otherwise), matching correct upstream behavior.

This miscalculates offsets used throughout reindentation (e.g. `_get_offset`), causing wrong indentation/newline decisions as seen in the parenthesis/where/identifier-list regressions. I'll fix the condition to break when the token matches (and yield otherwise), matching correct upstream behavior.
